submission.justification: Sensor-T2 gives the best unirradiated single-hit resolution of the three technologies (about 6.0-6.2 um across 100-200 um, versus 9.2 um for T3 and 14.0 um for T1 at 150 um). Within T2, resolution is flat between 100 and 200 um (5.98, 6.21, 6.15, 6.09 um at 100, 120, 150, 200 um; differences are close to the MC noise) and degrades at 300 um (7.6 um) and 50-80 um (6.9-6.6 um). I chose 200 um rather than the nominal minimum at 100 um because, after irradiation, collected charge scales with active thickness, so the thicker sensor should give more signal margin for the hard 97% efficiency requirement at 2e16 neq/cm^2, at no meaningful resolution cost. CAVEAT: the efficiency requirement could NOT be verified. The simulation tool only covers unirradiated resolution, and the project documents contain no irradiated charge-collection or efficiency data for any candidate. The efficiency status is therefore 'unknown', not 'met'. Before this recommendation is final, an irradiated (2e16 neq/cm^2) charge-collection and efficiency study for T2 at 200 um, with the operating bias and -35 C CO2 cooling, must confirm >=97%. If it fails, the fallback is Sensor-T1 (3D), which is expected to be more radiation tolerant but has about 2.3x worse resolution.

requirements.requirement: Sensor technology must be one of the three candidates in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Sensor-T2 is listed in candidate_specs.md (thin-pitch, large charge sharing).

requirements.requirement: Hit efficiency >= 97% up to end-of-life fluence 2e16 neq/cm^2 (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: No irradiated efficiency or charge-collection data exists in the documents or the simulation tool (tool is unirradiated only). Thicker T2 should retain more signal after irradiation, but this is not demonstrated. Requires irradiated simulation or test-beam verification before the design is final.

requirements.requirement: Best possible single-hit spatial resolution in the innermost layer (goal)
requirements.evidence: T2 at 200 um: 6.09 um unirradiated, vs 6.0 um at the 100 um optimum, 9.2 um for T3 and 14.0 um for T1 at 150 um. Resolution is within about 2% of the best achievable T2 value.
